title: Does my game looks polished enough to be released on Steam as-is?
author: Scorchyy

comments.author: CriticalMastery
comments.body: Meh, I thought it was a hentai puzzle game

replies.author: Scorchyy
replies.body: Maybe I should make that instead

comments.author: Guildbound
comments.body:
Tbh, no and this is why we get so much hate people want to release games like this and throw out to Steam thinking of if I sell it for $1-2 I’ll be rich if only couple thousand buy it.

Right now you have a playable demo which is nice now polish it, the graphics the stutters maybe add a main story line somewhere maybe figure out what makes ur game a lot more enjoyable than the rest and if not make it more enjoyable.

Find people to play it and see what they have to say etc etc

replies.author: Scorchyy
replies.body: Have you had any success on Steam yourself?

replies.author: Guildbound
replies.body:
I am still polishing my game, I had it just like you in placeholder version. Right now I have 30-40 players playing it and constantly throwing updates and fixes for things I didn’t know were broken when I made it so having real players test your game is very satisfying.

You don’t want those bugs to come out on release and have a bunch of negative reviews. I never stated I had success in Steam, just trying to help a fellow AI project developer reach his full potential.

I’m slowly trying to build a game I would play 100% not trying to dish out a game to solely publish on Steam. 

After all that is done you still have to market your game, you have two routes paid ads if you have the cash or natural engagement thru social media etc 

If you have any real questions like how to improve your game I’ll be more than happy to share all my tips and tricks. Tools etc I didn’t come here to bash your game but maybe open your eyes that if you think your game is good maybe it is but how so you know it’s good ?

comments.author: TechgeekOne
comments.body:
No honestly. I clicked the play button on the trailer and was immediately let down by the gameplay looking nothing like what the thumbnail suggested.

Consistency matters a ton when it comes to games. You want to hook the player into playing your game yes, but you also need to deliver something close to what they're expecting or they'll bail immediately.

replies.author: TechgeekOne
replies.body:
Some kind of card game or something with a significant focus on power-ups/upgrades and waifus. Which could work for your game but you'd need to adjust the art style to match. 

Your goal with a good trailer is to bring the player in anticipating something good, then build the desire to play the game enough that they take action. When you subvert their expectations (intentionally or implied) like that it has the opposite effect.
